title: fix: rebuild incomplete Git runtimes when source is current
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Git checkout can have the requested source commit and matching build provenance while still missing required runtime artifacts.
In that state, `openclaw update` currently takes the `already-current` shortcut instead of rebuilding.
The final safety check then rejects the incomplete runtime, leaving the operator with an update failure and no repair.
This completes the artifact checks for the source-current workflow covered by #156996.

## User Impact

A source-current checkout with missing build stamps, runtime entry, or Control UI startup assets now reaches the existing candidate build and validation path.
A complete checkout still skips core activation, and package-to-Git conversion still performs its required exposure work.
The existing service admission, external-supervisor guard, migration boundaries, and post-update maintenance remain in place.

Git status JSON also includes an optional `update.git.artifacts` observation with readiness and, when ready, the build identity and version.
The version comes from current build metadata, with the existing CLI package-version fallback when that metadata has no version.
The observation does not establish remote freshness, running Gateway health, candidate validation, or permission to restore state.
Package-install status remains unchanged, and no configuration or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater already computes complete native artifact verification, but its shortcut used only the recorded build commit.
Both the immediate target match and the fallback to the installed commit now use that existing verified result.
The artifact owner also produces the status observation so its version cannot drift to an edited source `package.json` while the installed build remains unchanged.

The patch preserves the separate `sourceRuntimePrepared` fact introduced by #158849 and its existing admission and finalization behavior.
Preferred-target reporting and external-manager client/UI changes are outside this PR.

## Evidence

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36248926130) passed, including production/test types, artifact/status tests, the corrected snapshot cases, and preferred-target status coverage.
The conflict-only replay after #158926 retains both status observation paragraphs and unchanged production/test edits.
Independent source review found no actionable defects.

The real-Git candidate tests cover incomplete-artifact repair, failed-candidate fallback, complete dev/stable/beta no-ops, package-to-Git exposure, and the existing `sourceRuntimePrepared` result.
They assert candidate build and validation before service stop.
The status fixture covers source-version drift, missing metadata, repeated artifact reads, and failed upstream fetches.

| Changed test file | Cloud macOS file wall time | CI test-case time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `update-check-status.test.ts` | 51.49 s, 33 passed | 3.261 s |
| `update-runner-git-candidate.test.ts` | 271.16 s, 64 passed | 17.258 s |
| `update-command-git-snapshot.test.ts` | 18.55 s, 3 passed | 5.915 s |

File runs used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; CI times sum reported case durations and exclude shard setup.
The three new artifact cases total 0.783 seconds in CI.
A separate execution-validation run passed all 23 cases in 11.38 seconds wall.
The ordered affected-suite run passed 164 tests and reproduced one workspace-runtime timeout, also reproduced on baseline `b4bcfe29678a` with current locked dependencies.
Standalone passes do not establish a fix for that ordered timeout.

### Published updater and real Gateway trace

The Linux proof used the actual npm `openclaw@2026.9.6` artifact, build commit `eb377ac59e6c`, with real Gateway processes behind the maintained systemd fixture.
Its prepared Git destination used normal locked dependencies and a task-owned Git remote pinned to tested source `aa515e53eb03`.
The final `1ac1f31ea954` replay preserves the artifact contribution; the related status composition was inspected and passed final-head CI.

| Driver and request | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Published driver, dirty Git destination | Refused; original Gateway PID 584 remained ready. |
| Published driver, clean destination | `status: ok`; native candidate build/activation replaced PID 584 with PID 9304 and verified build `2026.9.6-aa515e53eb03-2026-09-26T14-44-30.783Z`. |
| Candidate, missing runtime stamp, running fixture Gateway | Refused at existing `managed-service-preflight`; PID and readiness remained unchanged. |
| Candidate, missing runtime stamp, owner-stopped Gateway, `update --no-restart --json` | `status: ok`; real preflight build, unchanged source SHA, restored stamp, and new build `2026.9.6-aa515e53eb03-2026-09-26T14-52-44.871Z`; service remained inactive. |
| Repaired checkout, fresh task-owned service installation | Booted successfully and became ready; status reported `artifacts.ready: true` with the repaired build identity. |

The published driver cannot repair its own same-commit shortcut through candidate code; the corrected driver supplies that behavior after installation.
The fixture lacks native cgroup membership and complete enablement-policy observations, so the running candidate attempt and a later CLI start-wrapper attempt were safely blocked.
No guard was bypassed, and those attempts are not claimed as passing managed same-commit restart proof.
The successful same-commit repair used explicit owner quiescence; the subsequent boot used the same recorded repaired build and stamp in a fresh service fixture.
